batch_size_note: 500 units per rep. At 2000 units per rep this configuration outruns the Prefect server's event broker and the task-run recorder silently loses about half the task runs, so the database cannot account for every unit; 500 stays under that ceiling and all 6 reps recorded 500/500.
concurrency_mechanism: ThreadPoolTaskRunner(max_workers=20); 2000 @task .submit() calls inside one flow run. Tasks execute as threads of the flow's own process; nothing is queued server-side and no task is dispatched to a worker.
notes: Prefect's default execution path for @task. All 2000 futures are submitted before any result is awaited; submitting them takes under 0.2s. ThreadPoolTaskRunner is the default task runner, but its default max_workers is unbounded (sys.maxsize), so the 20-way cap is imposed by this experiment. task_run.created is written by the server's task-run recorder tens of seconds after the fact, so the per-unit submission anchor is the uuid7 that ThreadPoolTaskRunner.submit() mints at submission time; latency is that timestamp to the COMPLETED transition.
